s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic cough with intermittent paroxysmal episodes and associated sputum production, with a possible obstructive component
salient_findings: White viscous sputum production without bleeding
Obstructive pneumonia in the right lower lung
key_facts: 80-year-old Japanese man
7-month history of cough
Cough sometimes accompanied by white viscous sputum
Cough would become paroxysmal without triggers
Cough improved with periods of no symptoms
Medical history of myocardial infarction at age 68
Former smoker (2 packs/day for 48 years, quit at age 68)
Choking episode while eating yellowtail fish approximately 11 months prior to presentation
Vital signs: Temperature 35.9 °C, Blood pressure 126/64 mmHg, Heart rate 70 beats/min, Oxygen saturation 97% (room air)
Laboratory tests showed elevated white blood cell count and ALP
Chest radiograph showed slight increase in opacity in the right lower lung
Chest CT revealed obstructive pneumonia and a high-density structure
Bronchoscopy showed obstruction of the basal segmental bronchus's lumen
